text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- BRAZIL GETS READY TO FIGHT BARRIERS TO EXPORTS

A 65-page study about U.S. barriers to Brazilian exports of goods and services will be used by the Brazilian government as an important tool in negotiations with the U.S. and the World Trade Organization (WTO).
-- CEMENT COMPANIES HAVE LESS OWNERS; ACQUISITION WAVE IN THE SECTOR
The Dias family soon may give up control of cement company Cimentos Caue. The firm is on sale and at least two groups have showed interest in acquiring it: Ciminas and Votorantim group.
Since last year the cement industry has been experiencing the biggest wave of mergers and acquisitions of its history.
-- BANK AID PROGRAM LIKELY TO BE MAINTAINED

The government is likely to maintain in 1997 the special PROER credit lines for bank mergers and buyouts. The Central Bank believes the program is still necessary because the restructuring of the banking system has not been concluded yet. So far the PROER program has granted 14.4 billion reais to facilitate mergers of ailing banks.
-- MALUF IS NOT THE OWNER OF PPB, SAYS DORNELLES

Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles is against a party convention in which the Brazilian Progressist Party (PPB) would make a decision regarding the re-election amendment. Favorable to the amendment, Dornelles says Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf "is not the owner of the party."
-- INTERNATIONAL OLYMPIC COMMITTEE APPROVES RIO DE JANEIRO'S EFFORTS

Rio de Janeiro may not acquire the right for being the site of the Olympic Games in 2004, but at least in one item the city won a gold medal. The 19 members of the International Olympic Committee were impressed with how the Olympics project mobilized Rio people.

A study by the Interamerican Development Bank (IDB) sayss that Brazil should slow its economic growth to avoid crises. According to the IDB, the country is experiencing a "financial tension" period but shows signs that it can handle it.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
